text:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran the nightly perf suite after the kernel-selector tweak (optimize_for_small_batches=true). Observed a P99 regression on host_preparse: baseline 26.1ms -> canary 26.7ms (~2.3% / ~600us). P50 up ~1.1%. KV cache hit rate looks flat. Profiling attached (flame + stack samples): https://gist.github.com/redwood/abc123

josh: Which change exactly? kernel-selector or batching heuristics?

maria: kernel-selector (commit 5f3b2e0) — it prefers the smaller-kernel for batches < 16 to save GPU op cost. Hypothesis: that path triggers an extra code path in the tokenizer/parse-shim which added a guard around streaming chunk coalesce.

ryan: Can you paste the microbench command/output you ran locally?

maria: Sure:
```
$ bench_host_preparse --tokens=128 --qps=200 --trials=100
baseline: p50=8.3ms p95=18.7ms p99=26.1ms
canary:   p50=8.4ms p95=18.9ms p99=26.7ms
cpu-sample-top:
  22% tokenization::tokenize_bytes
  11% parse_shim::coalesce_chunks
   6% http2::frame_dispatch
```

anita: I also noticed more small syscalls in the flame — looks like extra memcpy/scan in the shim when the kernel choice flips. Could be due to a new fast-path guard that copies into a temp buffer.

josh: Does the new selector change KV cache codegen? Might affect KV cache warmup or layout -> extra misses? You said KV hit rate flat though. Any per-shard diff?

maria: KV hit rate aggregate unchanged (~98.7%), per-shard no clear delta. The samples point more to CPU work in host preparse rather than memory thrash.

ryan: I'll run an A/B on canary toggling the kernel pick to previous behavior (force_previous_kernel=true) and rerun the same bench. Pushing a quick patch to canary now.

ci-bot: Canary deploy started for tag canary-2026-03-21-5f3b2e0

ryan: Quick results after rollback toggle (canary): p99 back to 26.0ms (matches baseline). So regression is gated by selector path.

josh: Good repro. Two follow-ups: 1) quantify exact cost in tokenization when selector chooses small-kernel path, 2) consider moving the guard out of hot path or change guard to non-copy check.

maria: Agreed. I ran a narrow profiler with sampling enabled focused on tokenize_bytes and coalesce_chunks. The extra ~600us is ~420us in tokenize_bytes (extra loop) + ~180us in coalesce_chunks (extra boundary checks).

anita: I'll instrument the tokenizer to avoid temp buffer copy when input is single-buffer (common case). Patch idea: add fast-check if buffer_count==1 skip copy. Minimal change.

kevin: Also worth adding metric host_preparse_token_copy_count and alert if it increases >10% over baseline. I'll add to observability board.

maria: Action items:
- anita: implement no-copy fastcheck + unit tests on tokenizer (owner: anita)
- ryan: run full canary with selector=old vs selector=new and post perf delta + heap profile (owner: ryan)
- kevin: add metric for token copy count and dashboard + baseline (owner: kevin)
- josh: file a tweak in kernel-selector to avoid toggling kernel type for batch sizes 8-16 until we ship tokenizer fix (owner: josh)

anita: Will do. ETA EOD tomorrow for unit tests + microbench.

ryan: Full canary runs are queued — will post numbers here when done.

ci-bot: Canary job finished: host_preparse_p99 delta (new vs old) = +0.1ms after patch rollback; full traces in CI artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/job/1234/artifacts

maria: Thanks all. Moving this to follow-up board and opening a PR to hold selector change behind a flag until we get tokenizer no-copy. I'll tag owners per action items. :thumbsup:

josh: Thanks. Good catch, and nice quick rollback test.

kevin: I'll add the alert and dashboard tiles (token_copy_count, host_preparse_p99, kv_cache_hit_rate).

maria: Closing thread — will post PR link once opened.
